verses.zh: 主―万军之耶和华从耶路撒冷和犹大，除掉众人所倚靠的，所仗赖的，就是所倚靠的粮，所仗赖的水；
verses.en: Look, the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] is about to remove from Jerusalem[NOTE:2] and Judahevery source of security, including[NOTE:3] all the food and water,[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the master, the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, the “Lord of hosts”].” On the title “the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,” see the note at 1:9.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “support and support.” The masculine and feminine forms of the noun are placed side-by-side to emphasize completeness. See GKC 394 §122.v.
Heb “all the support of food, and all the support of water.”

verses.zh: 除掉勇士和战士，审判官和先知，占卜的和长老，
verses.en: the mighty men and warriors,judges and prophets,omen readers and leaders,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “elder” (so ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); NCV “older leaders.”

verses.zh: 五十夫长和尊贵人，谋士和有巧艺的，以及妙行法术的。
verses.en: captains of groups of 50,the respected citizens,[NOTE:1] advisers and those skilled in magical arts,[NOTE:2] and those who know incantations.
notes: Heb “the ones lifted up with respect to the face.” For another example of the Hebrew idiom, see 2 Kgs 5:1.

Heb “and the wise with respect to magic.” On the meaning of חֲרָשִׁים (kharashim, “magic”), see HALOT 358 s.v. III חרשׁ. Some understand here a homonym, meaning “craftsmen.” In this case, one could translate, “skilled craftsmen” (cf. NIV, NASB).

verses.zh: 主说：我必使孩童作他们的首领，使婴孩辖管他们。
verses.en: The Lord says,[NOTE:1] “I will make youths their officials;malicious young men[NOTE:2] will rule over them.
notes: The words “the Lord says” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The prophet speaks in vv. 1-3 (note the third person reference to the Lord in v. 1), but here the Lord himself announces that he will intervene in judgment. It is unclear where the Lord’s words end and the prophet’s pick up again. The prophet is apparently speaking again by v. 8, where the Lord is referred to in the third person. Since vv. 4-7 comprise a thematic unity, the quotation probably extends through v. 7.

תַעֲלוּלִים (taʿalulim) is often understood as an abstract plural meaning “wantonness, cruelty” (cf. NLT). In this case the chief characteristic of these leaders is substituted for the leaders themselves. However, several translations make the parallelism tighter by emending the form to עוֹלְלִים (ʿolelim, “children”; cf. ESV, NASB, NCV, NIV, NKJV, NRSV). This emendation is unnecessary for at least two reasons. The word in the MT highlights the cruelty or malice of the “leaders” who are left behind in the wake of God’s judgment. The immediate context makes clear the fact that they are mere youths. The coming judgment will sweep away the leaders, leaving a vacuum which will be filled by incompetent, inexperienced youths.

verses.zh: 百姓要彼此欺压；各人受邻舍的欺压。少年人必侮慢老年人；卑贱人必侮慢尊贵人。
verses.en: The people will treat each other harshly;men will oppose each other;neighbors will fight.[NOTE:1] Youths will proudly defy the elderlyand riffraff will challenge those who were once respected.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “man against man, and a man against his neighbor.”
Heb “and those lightly esteemed those who are respected.” The verb רָהַב (rahav) does double duty in the parallelism.

verses.zh: 人在父家拉住弟兄，说：你有衣服，可以作我们的官长。这败落的事归在你手下吧！
verses.en: Indeed, a man will grab his brotherright in his father’s house[NOTE:1] and say,[NOTE:2] ‘You own a coat—you be our leader!This heap of ruins will be under your control.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[in] the house of his father” (so ASV); NIV11 “in his father’s house.”
The words “and say” are supplied for stylistic reasons.
Heb “your hand”; NASB “under your charge.”sn The man’s motives are selfish. He tells his brother to assume leadership because he thinks he has some wealth to give away.

verses.zh: 那时，他必扬声说：我不作医治你们的人；因我家中没有粮食，也没有衣服，你们不可立我作百姓的官长。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the brother will shout,[NOTE:2] ‘I am no doctor,[NOTE:3] I have no food or coat in my house;don’t make me a leader of the people!’”
notes: Or “in that day” (KJV).
Heb “he will lift up [his voice].”
Heb “wrapper [of wounds]”; KJV, ASV, NRSV “healer.”

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷败落，犹大倾倒；因为他们的舌头和行为与耶和华反对，惹了他荣光的眼目。
verses.en: Jerusalem certainly stumbles,Judah falls,for their words and their actions offend the Lord;[NOTE:1] they rebel against his royal authority.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for their tongue and their deeds [are] to the Lord.”
Heb “to rebel [against] the eyes of his majesty.” The word כָּבוֹד (kavod) frequently refers to the Lord’s royal splendor that is an outward manifestation of his authority as king.

verses.zh: 他们的面色证明自己的不正；他们述说自己的罪恶，并不隐瞒，好像所多玛一样。他们有祸了！因为作恶自害。
verses.en: The look on their faces[NOTE:1] testifies to their guilt;[NOTE:2] like the people of Sodom they openly boast of their sin.[NOTE:3] Woe to them![NOTE:4] For they bring disaster on themselves.
notes: This refers to their proud, arrogant demeanor.
Heb “answers against them”; NRSV “bears witness against them.”
Heb “their sin, like Sodom, they declare, they do not conceal [it].”
Heb “woe to their soul.”

verses.zh: 你们要论义人说：他必享福乐，因为要吃自己行为所结的果子。
verses.en: Tell the innocent[NOTE:1] it will go well with them,[NOTE:2] for they will be rewarded for what they have done.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the righteous” (KJV, NASB, NIV, TEV); NLT “those who are godly.”
Heb “that it is good.”
Heb “for the fruit of their deeds they will eat.”

verses.zh: 恶人有祸了！他必遭灾难！因为要照自己手所行的受报应。
verses.en: Woe to the wicked sinners!For they will get exactly what they deserve.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for the work of his hands will be done to him.”

verses.zh: 至于我的百姓，孩童欺压他们，妇女辖管他们。我的百姓啊，引导你的使你走错，并毁坏你所行的道路。
verses.en: Oppressors treat my[NOTE:1] people cruelly;creditors rule over them.[NOTE:2] My people, your leaders mislead you;they give you confusing directions.[NOTE:3]
notes: This may refer to the prophet or to the Lord.

The Hebrew text appears to read literally, “My people, his oppressors, he deals severely, and women rule over them.” The correct text and precise meaning of the verse are debated. The translation above assumes (1) an emendation of נֹגְשָׂיו (nogesayv, “his oppressors”) to נֹגְשִׂים (nogeshim, “oppressors”) by moving the mem (ם) on the following form to the end of the word and dropping the vav (ו) as virtually dittographic; (2) an emendation of מְעוֹלֵל (meʿolel, a singular participle that does not agree with the preceding plural subject) to עֹלְלוּ (ʿolelu), a third plural Poel perfect from עָלַל (ʿalal, “deal severely”; note that the following form begins with a vav [ו]; the text may be haplographic or misdivided); and (3) an emendation (with support from the LXX) of נָשִׁים (nashim, “women”) to נֹשִׁים (noshim, “creditors”; a participle from נָשַׁא, nashaʾ). Another option is to emend מְעוֹלֵל to עוֹלְלִים (ʿolelim, “children”) and read, “My people’s oppressors are children; women rule over them.” In this case the point is the same as in v. 4; the leadership void left by the judgment will be filled by those incompetent to lead the community—children and women.
Heb “and the way of your paths they confuse.” The verb בָּלַע (balaʿ, “confuse”; HALOT 135 s.v. I בלע) is a homonym of the more common בָּלַע (“swallow”; see HALOT 134 s.v. בלע).

verses.zh: 耶和华起来辩论，站着审判众民。
verses.en: The Lord takes his position to judge;he stands up to pass sentence on his people.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text has עַמִּים (ʿammim, “nations”) but the context makes it clear that the Lord is judging his covenant people. As indicated by the LXX the text should read עַמּוֹ (ʿammo, “his people”). The final mem (ם) on the form in the Hebrew is either dittographic or enclitic. When the mem was added or read as a plural ending, the vav (ו) was then misread as a yod (י).

verses.zh: 耶和华必审问他民中的长老和首领，说：吃尽葡萄园果子的就是你们；向贫穷人所夺的都在你们家中。
verses.en: The Lord comes to pronounce judgment on the leaders of his people and their officials.He says,[NOTE:1] “It is you[NOTE:2] who have ruined[NOTE:3] the vineyard![NOTE:4] You have stashed in your houses what you have stolen from the poor.[NOTE:5]
notes: The words “he says” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The pronominal element is masculine plural; the leaders are addressed.
The verb בָּעַר (baʿar, “graze, ruin”; HALOT 146 s.v. II בער) is a homonym of the more common בָּעַר (baʿar, “burn”; see HALOT 145 s.v. I בער).
The vineyard is a metaphor for the nation here. See 5:1-7.
Heb “the plunder of the poor [is] in your houses” (so NASB).

verses.zh: 主―万军之耶和华说：你们为何压制我的百姓，搓磨贫穷人的脸呢？
verses.en: Why do you crush my peopleand grind the faces of the poor?”[NOTE:1] The Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:2] has spoken.
notes: The rhetorical question expresses the Lord’s outrage at what the leaders have done to the poor. He finds it almost unbelievable that they would have the audacity to treat his people in this manner.

Heb Traditionally, the “Lord of hosts.” On the title “the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,” see the note at 1:9.sn The use of this title, which also appears in v. 1, forms an inclusio around vv. 1-15. The speech begins and ends with a reference to “the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies.”

verses.zh: 耶和华又说：因为锡安的女子狂傲，行走挺项，卖弄眼目，俏步徐行，脚下玎璫，
verses.en: The Lord says,“The women[NOTE:1] of Zion are proud.They walk with their heads high[NOTE:2] and flirt with their eyes.They skip along[NOTE:3] and the jewelry on their ankles jingles.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “daughters” (so KJV, NAB, NRSV).
Heb “with an outstretched neck.” They proudly hold their heads high so that others can see the jewelry around their necks.
Heb “walking and skipping, they walk.”
Heb “and with their feet they jingle.”

verses.zh: 所以，主必使锡安的女子头长秃疮；耶和华又使她们赤露下体。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the Lord[NOTE:2] will afflict the foreheads of Zion’s women[NOTE:3] with skin diseases;[NOTE:4] the Lord will make the front of their heads bald.”[NOTE:5]
notes: In the Hebrew text vv. 16-17 are one long sentence, “Because the daughters of Zion are proud and walk…, the Lord will afflict….” In v. 17 the Lord refers to himself in the third person.
The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here and in v. 18 is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “the daughters of Zion.”
Or “a scab” (KJV, ASV); NIV, NCV, CEV “sores.”

The precise meaning of this line is unclear because of the presence of the rare word פֹּת (pot). Since the verb in the line means “lay bare, make naked,” some take פֹּת as a reference to the genitals (cf. KJV, ASV, NRSV, CEV). (In 1 Kgs 7:50 a noun פֹּת appears, with the apparent meaning “socket.”) J. N. Oswalt (Isaiah [NICOT], 1:139, n. 2), basing his argument on alleged Akkadian evidence and the parallelism of the verse, takes פֹּת as “forehead.”

verses.zh: 到那日，主必除掉她们华美的脚钏、发网、月牙圈、
verses.en: [NOTE:1] At that time[NOTE:2] the Lord will remove their beautiful ankle jewelry,[NOTE:3] neck ornaments, crescent-shaped ornaments,
notes: The translation assumes that the direct quotation ends with v. 17. The introductory formula “in that day” and the shift from a poetic to prosaic style indicate that a new speech unit begins in v. 18.
Or “in that day” (KJV).
Or “the beauty of [their] ankle jewelry.”

verses.zh: 耳环、手镯、蒙脸的帕子、
verses.en: earrings, bracelets, veils,

verses.zh: 华冠、足链、华带、香盒、符囊、
verses.en: headdresses, ankle ornaments, sashes, sachets,[NOTE:1] amulets,
notes: Heb “houses of breath.” HALOT 124 s.v. בַּיִת defines them as “scent-bottles”; cf. NAB, NRSV “perfume boxes.”

verses.zh: 戒指、鼻环、
verses.en: rings, nose rings,

verses.zh: 吉服、外套、云肩、荷包、
verses.en: festive dresses, robes, shawls, purses,

verses.zh: 手镜、细麻衣、裹头巾、蒙身的帕子。
verses.en: garments, vests, head coverings, and gowns.[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical purpose for such a lengthy list is to impress on the audience the guilt of these women with their proud, materialistic attitude, whose husbands and fathers have profited at the expense of the poor.tn The precise meaning of many of the words in this list is uncertain.

verses.zh: 必有臭烂代替馨香，绳子代替腰带，光秃代替美发，麻衣系腰代替华服，烙伤代替美容。
verses.en: A putrid stench will replace the smell of spices,[NOTE:1] a rope will replace a belt,baldness will replace braided locks of hair,a sackcloth garment will replace a fine robe,and a prisoner’s brand will replace beauty.
notes: Heb “and it will be in place of spices there will be a stench.” The nouns for “spices” and “stench” are right next to each other in the MT for emphatic contrast. The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 你的男丁必倒在刀下；你的勇士必死在阵上。
verses.en: Your[NOTE:1] men will fall by the sword,your strong men will die in battle.[NOTE:2]
notes: The pronoun is feminine singular, suggesting personified Zion, as representative of its women, is the addressee. The reference to “her gates’ in v. 26 makes this identification almost certain.
Heb “your strength in battle.” The verb in the first clause provides the verbal idea for the second clause.

verses.zh: 锡安（原文是她）的城门必悲伤、哀号；她必荒凉坐在地上。
verses.en: Her gates will mourn and lament;deprived of her people, she will sit on the ground.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “she will be empty, on the ground she will sit.” Jerusalem is personified as a destitute woman who sits mourning the empty city.
